translation_notes: three graphs in one function, so no `@graph` can be declared: every island carries the call suffix instead -- `m{ ... }(in_second)`, `+{ ... }(in_both)`, `-{ ... }(in_first)`, `-{ ... }(in_second)`. This is the case the call suffix was made for, and it reads well; the receiver moves from the head of the statement to its tail

NEGATIVE for the stratum: none of the two `.remove()` here is a wildcard -- both remove a fully ground triple -- so this region exercises `-{ }` but NOT the joker. The stratum's sampling is by call site, not by the presence of a None

`in_second.value(s, p)` -> `m{ {s} {p} ?o_2 }(in_second).first()` (trav_single_value). Nuance: rdflib's value(any=True) returns an ARBITRARY object when several exist, and .first() the first the store yields -- neither is specified. The fixtures keep every (s, p) functional so the comparison is deterministic; a multi-valued (s, p) would make the region itself ambiguous, not the translation

`for s, p, o in list(in_first)` -> `for s, p, o in list(m{ ?s ?p ?o }(in_first))`: the most specific construction for a full scan, and it is LONGER than the Python form (three variables the original does not name). Recorded as a cost, not a gain: `m{ }` pays on a selective pattern, not on iterating a whole graph

oracle values (corpus/405): the region reads AND mutates three graphs, so it needs two Turtle inputs -- fixture.ttl (in_first) and fixture_second.ttl (in_second), in_both starting empty. run_pair(fixture=..., calls=[...]) parses both fresh per side and compares the three graphs left behind by isomorphism (the function returns None)

the fixtures cover: three decimal pairs to move (equal value, different lexical form -- the bug the filter exists for -- plus one identical pair), a decimal pair whose values DIFFER, the zero-solution case (no (s, p) in in_second, so .value()/.first() must both answer None, once under a URI subject and once under a blank node), and neighbours that must not match: an xsd:integer pair, a plain literal, a URIRef object (isinstance(o, Literal) rejects it), and triples of in_second with no counterpart at all. Mutation-checked: writing {o_2} instead of {o} into in_both, or removing from the wrong graph, is caught

repair.driver: fixture.ttl et fixture_second.ttl enrichis (le driver.py n'a gagné que sa docstring) : voisins qui partagent un terme d'un triplet déplacé sans en être un (obs1 ex:alt : même sujet et même objet, autre prédicat ; obs10 en in_first et obs11 en in_second : même prédicat et même objet, autre sujet ; obs14 en in_first : même sujet et prédicat, autre objet 8.5 ; obs2 ex:alt en in_second ; obs15 : deux décimaux égaux 6.0 et 6.00 en in_second pour un même couple), et deux paires entier/décimal de même valeur numérique (obs12, obs13 ; Decimal(2) == 2) qui rendent observables les deux tests de datatype.
repair.remaining: Le couple (s, p) de obs15 est multi-valué dans in_second, donc `.value()` / `.first()` y rendent l'« premier objet du magasin » (non spécifié) ; les deux objets sont des décimaux de même valeur pour que la région reste déterministe quel que soit celui lu, mais l'ordre du magasin reste une hypothèse commune aux deux côtés. Le jugement sur la région (aucun joker réel dans le `-{ }`, `m{ }` plus long que `list(in_first)`) revient à Maxime.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the nested ifs merge into one condition; `o_2 is not None` goes (isinstance(o_2, Literal) excludes None); the two datatype tests become the chained `o.datatype == o_2.datatype == XSD.decimal`. The order of the side-effect-free tests changes, not their result.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `in_second.value(s, p)` -> `m{ {s} {p} ?o_2 }(in_second).first()`, the add and the two removes as `+{ }(in_both)`, `-{ }(in_first)`, `-{ }(in_second)` (three graphs, so call suffixes and no @graph), `xsd:decimal`. The scan stays `list(in_first)`: the translation's `list(m{ ?s ?p ?o }(in_first))` is longer and adds nothing. No exception to the symmetry rule.

The notation costs here (ratio above 1): every island is a one-for-one replacement of a short rdflib call on a graph named by a variable, and m{ }.first() with an interpolated subject and predicate is longer than .value(s, p). Both removes are fully bound, so -{ } brings no wildcard to win on.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: nothing unused (Graph in the annotations, Literal, XSD), a copy of optimized.py.
optimized_header.ldpy: XSD goes from the rdflib import (replaced by @prefix xsd:).
